To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Swedish randomized trials of mammographic screening have shown a significant reduction in the breast cancer mortality of screened women compared with the control group.
screening with mammography in women aged 50-74 years, with an invitation interval of 2 years, reduces breast cancer mortality by 20% (range 15-25%) in women with 100% attendance.
the reduction in the risk of death due to breast cancer is about 20% and that the risk of dying from other causes is increased in women who are screened.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the mammography screening program on mortality from breast cancer.
the effects of breast screening on breast cancer mortality.
the development of a new approach for the evaluation of breast cancer screening.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Swedish trials showed a 30 % reduction in the mortality rate from breast cancer in women aged 40-69 years who were invited for screening and who accepted the invitation.
there is a 20-30% reduction in the risk of dying from breast cancer in women who have accepted screening compared to women who have not accepted screening.

the evidence from randomised trials is that breast cancer mortality is reduced by about 25% in women aged 40-70 years after about 5 years of follow-up, assuming that those who do and those who do not attend screening have the same risk of dying from breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
screening for breast cancer with mammography in women 40 to 49 years of age reduces mortality with 15% to 25%.
screening reduces the risk of dying from breast cancer.
the Swedish trials have provided convincing evidence that breast cancer mortality is reduced by screening mammography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk reduction is not as great as the 20% to 30% that is often quoted.

we can use the data from mammography screening trials to provide a more accurate estimate of how many lives are saved by mammography screening, and we can use the same data to determine how many lives are needlessly lost due to the harms of screening.
the current screening mammography guidelines are not based on evidence.
